name.en: Elpistostege — articulated fossil and fin study
name.zh: 希望螈鱼（完整化石与胸鳍研究）

scope: Original flattened near-tetrapod fish fossil with preserved digit-bearing fin anatomy, MHNM06-2067-informed study. A volumetric low-poly fossil relief with genuine discrete fin elements, not a photograph/painted plane and not a free-standing living animal.

scale.status: Published specimen total length, Nature2020 abstract. Fig1a scale1m; fin Figs2–3 scales5cm.
scale.uncertainty: Slab geometry and relief depth are artist-controlled support dimensions, not measured original slab thickness. Preserve body/fin scale relationship.

material_policy: Neutral warm-brown fossil against grey thin matrix, modest light-bone contrast in analytical fin reveal. Opaque palette only, no reference image texture.
diagnostic_targets: Broad triangular flattened skull with paired dorsal eye positions; long tapering articulated body, caudal tail and preserved fin regions as Fig1a/b.
Low relief three-dimensional skull/body/scales and tail rays, not a flat silhouette decal. Do not add a dorsal fin absent from reference.
Near-shoulder pectoral fins are separate from much farther posterior pelvic fins.

One integrated pectoral fin endoskeleton reveal must show humerus branching into distinct radius/ulna, then smaller wrist-like elements and multiple distal radial rows with digit-like elements, within the fin outline. Use Fig3d as preserved CT relation; do not turn this into a human five-fingered hand.
Fine lepidotrichial rays remain beyond/around internal endoskeleton; digits stay enclosed in fin, not external toes.
Bone relief elements maintain real gaps and anatomical sequence. Do not replace distal radials with generic parallel ribs.
reveal_policy: Analytical visualization: pectoral fins are naturally visible ventrally (Fig1 caption), and the endoskeleton was CT-revealed (Fig3). This model deliberately reveals one pectoral interior in its in-situ location for study; disclose this is a virtual cutaway and not naturally exposed dorsal fossil preservation. Preserve whole specimen and in-situ scale, no oversized detached hand prop.
uncertainties: Original fossil is compressed; low-poly relief height and soft connecting silhouette are representational.
Fig3e attempts restoration of compressed element shapes; prefer Fig3d actual CT configuration rather than silently claiming restored bones are exact.
Fine scale/ray counts simplified; no scientific claim of pixel-accurate CT segmentation.
acceptance_checklist: Original601 fossil-study scope retained: full flattened fish plus diagnostic digit-bearing fin anatomy.
Top/perspective clearly show cutaway anatomy without a separate enlarged floating prop.
Humerus/radius/ulna sequence and branching distal elements are individually readable; no generic hand or toes.
Mesh relief with nonzero depth and real gaps; no photo-plane substitution.
Relative fin/body scale follows reference5cm and1m bars.
Default4 exact-GLB views, standard checks and two rebuilds, independent review separate.
